title: Media & Embedding
description: Bring your pages to life with audio, video, SVG, responsive images, and embedded third-party content. Learn the modern HTML media toolkit used in every professional web project.
learningObjectives: Embed video and audio with native HTML5 players
Use iframe to embed YouTube, maps, and other external content
Implement responsive images with picture and srcset
Use SVG inline and as img src
Understand performance implications of media elements

sections.content: Native HTML5 Video

The <video> element lets you embed video directly without plugins. Add the controls attribute to show the built-in play/pause/volume buttons. You can provide multiple <source> elements with different formats so the browser picks the one it supports.
💡 Key attributes: controls (show UI), autoplay (auto-start), muted (start muted), loop (repeat), poster (thumbnail before play), preload (none/metadata/auto).

<!-- Autoplaying background video (muted is required!) -->
<video autoplay muted loop playsinline>
  <source src="hero-bg.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
</video>
⚠️ Browsers block autoplay with sound. If you need autoplay, always add muted — otherwise it will be silently blocked.

exercises.question: Which video attribute is required for autoplay to work in most modern browsers?
hints: Browsers protect users from surprise audio
exercises.explanation: Modern browsers block autoplaying video with sound to prevent jarring user experiences. Adding muted bypasses this restriction.

sections.content: Embedding Audio
The <audio> element works identically to <video> but for sound. Provide multiple source formats (MP3 and OGG) for maximum browser support. Add controls to show the built-in player.
🎯 Always include fallback content inside video and audio for browsers that don't support them, and for SEO.

exercises.question: Write an audio player for 'episode01.mp3' with controls. Include an OGG fallback source and a download link as fallback content.
exercises.explanation: Multiple source elements let the browser pick the first format it can play. The fallback paragraph appears in browsers that don't support audio.

sections.content: What is an iframe?

The <iframe> (inline frame) embeds another HTML page inside your page. It's how YouTube videos, Google Maps, Twitter widgets, and payment forms (Stripe, PayPal) are embedded. The src attribute specifies the URL to embed.

<!-- Embed a YouTube video -->
<iframe
  width="560"
  height="315"
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
  title="YouTube video player"
  frameborder="0"
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
  allowfullscreen
></iframe>

<!-- Google Maps -->
<iframe
  src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=..."
  width="600"
  height="450"
  allowfullscreen
  loading="lazy"
  title="Office location on Google Maps"
></iframe>
⚠️ Security: Never embed untrusted content in an iframe. Add sandbox attribute to restrict capabilities: <iframe sandbox='allow-scripts'>
🎯 Always add a descriptive title attribute to iframes — screen readers announce it to users.

exercises.question: Which attribute makes an iframe load only when it's near the viewport, improving page performance?
hints: The same attribute works on images too
exercises.explanation: loading='lazy' defers loading until the element is near the viewport. This significantly improves initial page load time when you have multiple iframes.

sections.content: Why Responsive Images?
Sending a 4000px wide image to a 375px phone wastes bandwidth and slows load times. Responsive images let the browser select the most appropriate image size for the current device.
srcset — Serving Different Resolutions
picture — Art Direction

The <picture> element lets you serve completely different images at different breakpoints — not just different resolutions of the same image. Use it for art direction (cropping differently for mobile vs desktop) and format switching (WebP vs JPEG).

exercises.question: Which element would you use to serve a WebP image to supported browsers and fall back to JPEG for others?
hints: This element supports multiple source formats
exercises.explanation: with lets modern browsers use the efficient WebP format while an fallback serves JPEG to older browsers.

sections.content: What is SVG?

SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is an XML-based image format that scales to any size without losing quality. Unlike JPEG or PNG (raster images made of pixels), SVG describes shapes mathematically. It's perfect for logos, icons, illustrations, and charts.
Using SVG in HTML
🎯 Use inline SVG for icons you want to style with CSS (color, size, hover effects). Use for static logos where you don't need CSS control.
Accessible SVGs

<!-- Decorative icon (hide from screen readers) -->
<svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
  <!-- paths -->
</svg>

<!-- Meaningful SVG (needs a title) -->
<svg role="img" aria-labelledby="icon-title">
  <title id="icon-title">Search</title>
  <!-- paths -->
</svg>

exercises.question: Which method of including an SVG allows you to change its color using CSS?
hints: CSS can only style elements in the same document
exercises.explanation: Inline SVG is part of the HTML document, so CSS and JavaScript can access and modify its elements. External SVGs loaded via img or CSS background are sandboxed.

capstoneProject.title: Portfolio with Media
capstoneProject.description: Build a rich portfolio page that showcases a hero video, a projects gallery with responsive images, embedded demo videos, and an SVG icon system.
requirements: An autoplaying muted loop hero video
At least 3 project cards each with a responsive <picture> image
An embedded YouTube demo video using iframe
At least 3 inline SVG icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, external link)
An audio player for a 'podcast/presentation' section
All media has proper alt/title for accessibility
loading='lazy' on all below-fold images and iframes
